findings.title: Section 6 resolves function/class endpoints while the read discipline forbids reading those nodes
findings.description:
Section 6 states that "Function- and class-level edge endpoints are resolved to their owning file's layer rather than dropped, so a `calls` edge between two functions in different layers still counts as an inter-layer signal" (lines 215-219). But the same document's **Read discipline, unchanged** section (lines 282-293) says the 687 function/class nodes "remain excluded and are the reason the discipline exists," Success Criterion 9 (lines 331-333) requires that "no function- or class-level node is read," and walkthrough step 7 (lines 437-440) requires confirming "no function/class-level node data appears in any section." The architecture's read discipline is equally explicit: "File-level node types … are sufficient for planning artifacts; function- and class-level nodes are not read."

The design never names the mechanism that reconciles these. Two compliant mechanisms exist — deriving the owning path from the type-prefixed node id (`function:path:name`, per the architecture's node-id convention) or mapping endpoints through `contains` edges — but the obvious implementation (looking up the node's `filePath`) is exactly what SC9 forbids. The design's own verification snippet compounds the ambiguity: the walkthrough step-1 `jq` at lines 351-353 builds a `from_entries` map over `[.nodes[]|{name:.id,value:.type}]`, i.e. it indexes the id and type of all 925 nodes including the 687 function/class ones. Specify the endpoint-resolution mechanism explicitly and either reconcile or restate SC9 in terms of what is actually permitted (e.g. "no function/class node record is read; ids are parsed").

findings.title: Empty `.understandignore` fallback conflicts between the binding mapping row and the section detail
findings.description: Row 7 of the extraction mapping (line 180) is binding — "on absence emits that fallback and nothing else" (lines 172-173) — and gives, for absent/empty, `[GAP: ...]` "naming the unreadable file." The section-7 detail (lines 232-235) says an all-comments `.understandignore` "is reported as 'defaults only', not as a gap." These are the same case (a file readable but empty of active patterns) with two different required outputs, and the row's gap text ("the unreadable file") is wrong for a readable-but-empty file. The detail also conflates three distinct states — file absent/unreadable, file with zero active patterns, and optional `config.json` keys absent — under one rule; the third is separately and correctly ruled out as a gap (lines 228-231). Additionally, the parenthetical "(this repo's current state has 17 active lines)" sits inside the all-comments sentence while the Verified graph facts table (line 108) and walkthrough spot-check (line 389) both record 17 *active* lines — so this repo is not the all-comments case the sentence describes. Split row 7's fallback per input and per state (absent/unreadable → gap; zero active patterns → "defaults only") and fix the parenthetical.

findings.title: `edges[].direction` is declared as consumed but appears in no section's source fields
findings.description: The Interfaces Required table (line 86) lists `edges[].weight`, `.direction` for "Dependency ordering," but mapping row 6 (line 179) names only `type`, `source`, `target`, `weight`, and the section-6 detail never uses `direction`. Success Criterion 1 requires every section to name its fields "matching the extraction mapping table," so a field consumed outside the table cannot be named. Either drop `direction` from the interfaces table or add it to row 6 with its role.

findings.title: Correction 2 describes the binding selector as both an allow-list and an exclusion
findings.description: Line 151 says "the file-level selector becomes an explicit type allow-list," and line 158 says "Stated as an exclusion rather than an allow-list deliberately." The emitted rule (`select(.type != "function" and .type != "class")`, lines 155-157) is unambiguous and its rationale is sound, so this is a wording defect only — but it sits in the paragraph defining the selector that Success Criterion 5 makes binding, and the design's own standard for this document is precision about what is binding. Reword line 151 to call it an exclusion filter. (The same loose "unchanged … gains only a cross-reference line" phrasing around the `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` decision at lines 258/277 vs. SC7 is a milder instance of the same pattern; SC7 states the edit correctly.)
